title: Literature Review and Evidence Synthesis
answer: Evidence extraction, weighing the consensus, questions over your own sources, broad scans and translating between fields.

children.name: Evidence Extraction Tables
children.blurb: Evidence extraction tables are structured summaries that pull key claims, study designs, populations, interventions, outcomes, and effect sizes from primary research into a comparable grid.

children.name: Weighing the Scientific Consensus
children.blurb: Weighing the scientific consensus means assessing how much agreement exists across a body of research on a specific question.

children.name: Questioning Your Own Sources
children.blurb: Questioning your own sources is the practice of checking the origin, methods, funding, and current status of every work you cite before treating it as evidence.

children.name: Deep Research Agents and Landscape Scans
children.blurb: Deep research agents are software systems that carry out multi-step literature search, reading, and synthesis tasks, producing landscape scans that map a field's key papers, claims, models, tools, and open questions.

children.name: Translating Between Disciplines
children.blurb: Translating between disciplines in literature review and evidence synthesis means identifying equivalent concepts, methods, and findings across fields that use different vocabularies, and mapping them so evidence can be combined.

sections.body: This field covers using AI to pull evidence out of research, compare findings, check sources, scan broadly, and connect ideas across fields. In practice, AI systems now read papers and produce structured tables of claims, methods, and results. They can flag where studies agree or disagree, and they can retrieve related work from large collections. The work is not about generating new evidence but about organizing and summarizing what already exists. For example, a tool might take a set of papers on a topic and list each study's sample size, outcome, and limitations. This helps a researcher see the shape of a literature without reading every paper first.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The basic extraction of claims from clean, well formatted papers is fairly reliable, but it still misses nuance in complex arguments or figures. Weighing a scientific consensus is only partly solved: AI can count and cluster findings, but it cannot yet judge quality the way a careful human reviewer can. Questioning sources remains hard because AI tends to trust the text it is given and may not notice conflicts of interest or weak methods unless they are spelled out. Broad scans work for known topics but often return too much or too little when a field uses different words for the same idea. Translating between disciplines is still early; AI can suggest analogies but often gets technical meanings wrong. The honest limit is that these tools reduce reading time, not the need for expert judgment.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages in this section move from concrete extraction to broader synthesis. Evidence Extraction Tables shows how AI turns papers into structured rows and columns, which is the starting point for any review. Weighing the Scientific Consensus then takes those extracted claims and asks how much agreement actually exists, and where the disagreements are. Questioning Your Own Sources steps back to examine the papers themselves, including funding, methods, and possible bias. Deep Research Agents and Landscape Scans widens the view to find work across a whole field, not just the papers you already have. Translating Between Disciplines closes the loop by helping a reader carry findings from one area into another without losing meaning. A reader would start with the first page for mechanics, then move through the others as their review grows from a single question to a full map of evidence.
